newsitem.title: USA: CAI, ADC in 2-way wireless pact.
newsitem.headline: CAI, ADC in 2-way wireless pact.

text.p: CAI Wireless Systems Inc said Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding with telecom equipment maker ADC Telecommunications Inc to develop a two-way broadband communications system to transmit video, voice and data using CAI's wireless technology.
The company said that, subject to regulatory approval, it expected to begin testing the new system in Pittsburgh "sometime during the first calendar quarter of 1997."
CAI said it is now in negotiation with various service providers and equipment vendors to help deliver its two-way transmission services.

CAI said that, subject to the results of the tests in Pittsburgh, the companies plan to deploy a demonstration system in the Boston region, where last week CAI received permanent fixed two-way permits at 16 sites from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.
It said that further development would be the subject of a definitive written agreement yet to be negotiated.
CAI and ADC's two-way broadband wireless system will use ADC's Homeworx platform and CAI's Multichannel Multipoint Distribution Services (MMDS) radio spectrum licenses.
CAI said it will apply to the FCC for fixed two-way wireless transmission authority in Pittsburgh.

The company said it has already received limited approvals from the FCC for similar developments in other markets, including permanent authorization in Boston and developmental authorization in Hartford, Conn.
It said the system could be used as an alternative means of delivering Internet access and subscription television.
Company officials at CAI and ADC said the system under development is expected to support a broad array of video, voice and data communications services when completed.
These would include wireless high capacity services such as T-1, Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) and wireless multipoint video distribution.

Wireless communications companies like CAI have traditionally used its wireless radio spectrum, which comprises microwave frequencies rather than traditional hard-wired cable, to deliver video programming services.

CAI has sought regulatory approval to expand use of MMDS spectrum for services like high-speed Internet and Intranet access, home shopping and banking, and subscription television alternatives to residential consumers and businesses.

It said small and mid-sized businesses, which often cannot negotiate competitive service prices the way large corporations can, could be the biggest beneficiaries of fixed two-way wireless communications services.

CAI is also testing high-speed Internet access services in New York City and Rochester, N.Y. It also has a portfolio of MMDS wireless channel rights in eight markets in the Northeast and Middle Atlantic regions of the United States.

In May 1995, Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp agreed to invest $100 million in CAI Wireless in exchange for a 20 percent stake in the company. The companies had said they planned to offer wireless cable services using CAI spectrum.
CAI stock had gained 18/32 to 2-7/32 in early trading Monday.
